solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I don't know where ship may be heading, or what passenger may need?

parts.note: in a quiz, a contestant stumped by a question says 'pass'
a ship heads for a port, its harbour destination

explanation.surface: A puzzled traveller confesses ignorance of the ship's destination, or asks what a passenger needs to bring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as a single question about a voyage; it is two pieces, a quiz contestant's word for giving up and a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: An international traveller needs this travel document to cross borders, so a passenger may well need one.

clue.text: Optimist's carpet acquiring shine

definitions.note: Optimist's is read as 'optimist is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for carpet gets the word for shine added on

parts.note: to carpet is to reprimand; to pan is to criticise harshly
gloss is a shine or lustre

explanation.surface: A rug that someone optimistic owns picks up a shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is a verb, to scold, as in being 'carpeted' by the boss; Dr Pangloss is the relentless optimist in Voltaire's Candide.
explanation.definitionFit: The tutor in Voltaire's Candide insists all is for the best, so his name means a naive optimist.

clue.text: All dwarfs, small and equal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
even means equal or level

explanation.surface: Every dwarf is little and of the same height.
explanation.walkthrough: Snow White's dwarfs number seven, so 'All dwarfs' is their total.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Snow White tale there are exactly this many dwarfs, so the number counts all of them.

clue.text: Swine bagged first in physics, gold mark in college

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of the word physics

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: in places the word for mark inside the college name

parts.note: King's is a Cambridge college
a scratch is a mark on a surface

explanation.surface: A pig snatched a first in physics and a gold medal at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine bagged' is pig sold in packets: these crisp fried pig-skin pieces are a classic British pub snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Crunchy fried pork rind sold in small packets in pubs is swine meat, bagged for sale.

clue.text: Stop the music

definitions.meaning: to stop oneself from doing something, to desist
a repeated chorus line in a song or poem

explanation.surface: An order to halt the band.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to abstain, and as a noun it is the chorus repeated in a song.

clue.text: Correspondence course's leader wearing a tie

indicators.note: the pair of words 'a tie' wear the leading letter like a garment, holding it inside them

parts.note: a cord is a string used to tie something

indicators.note: the leader of the word course's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A letter-writing course's head turns up dressed in a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts C, the first letter of 'course's', between A and CORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of agreement or harmony between things is a synonym of this word for concord.

clue.text: Conservative icon gets Labour rattled, almost

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Tory figurehead nearly unsettles the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' seems to describe Labour's mood; it is the anagram signal for ICON GETS LABOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from fairground games that gave a cigar as a prize, describes narrowly missing success.

clue.text: Large plant as it happens in books, always coming up

indicators.note: in puts the broadcasting word inside the abbreviation for the books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a broadcast as it happens is live

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the poetic word for always is read upwards

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A big plant shows up, as it happens, in books for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean fruit tree grows large and lives for centuries, so it is a large plant.

clue.text: Process like the litmus test ends

parts.note: in slang, to dig something is to like it

indicators.note: ends picks the closing letter of each of the words the, litmus and test

explanation.surface: A procedure resembling the litmus test in chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like 'similar to'; it is the verb, slang DIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb information or food is to break it down and take it in, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Capital letters reading across from left of keyboard?

definitions.text: Capital letters reading across from left of keyboard?

parts.words: Capital letters reading across from left of keyboard?
parts.note: describe the leftmost keys of the middle row of a typewriter keyboard, read in order from one key to the next, as the name of a capital city

explanation.surface: A typing lesson on reading the capital letters along the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital letters' suggests upper case; 'Capital' is the city, and reading the keys one after the other in words gives its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital's name sounds out the first two keys of the home row with the word between them.

clue.text: No way in, game finally remarkably short

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the words in and game
short means the word for remarkably loses its last letter

parts.note: remarkably good means very good

explanation.surface: Someone refuses outright to join in, since the game finishes oddly early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' applies to both 'in' and 'game', giving N and E; 'short' cuts VERY to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'no way' is an emphatic refusal, the same as saying not at any time whatever.

clue.text: Out of shape, seeking familiar place — working out

parts.note: someone out of shape is unfit, perhaps overweight or fat
a homing pigeon seeks its home, the familiar place

explanation.surface: An unfit person looks for a familiar gym to start exercising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like exercise, fitting 'Out of shape'; it means figuring out.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of a problem, as by measuring the depth of water, is to understand or solve it.

clue.text: Painting clasped, an original

indicators.note: original here means novel or freshly made, so the letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A painting is gripped tightly, being an original rather than a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' is the anagram signal, not a description of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of rural scenery, countryside and fields, is a genre of picture named for that view.

clue.text: Chiefs formerly cross, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the spoken form of 'formerly cross' gives the letters

parts.note: formerly is EX and a cross is the letter X, spoken ex-ex

explanation.surface: Bosses who used to be angry, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Formerly is EX- (as in ex-wife) and a cross is the letter X, also said 'ex'.
explanation.definitionFit: Executives, shortened in business slang, are the heads or leaders of a company.

clue.text: Orange-yellow salve initially applied to slight cut

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word salve
cut means the synonym for slight is docked at its end

parts.note: as a noun, a slight is an insult or affront

explanation.surface: A soothing ointment is first spread on a small wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight cut' reads as a small wound; slight is a noun (an affront) and 'cut' drops its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice from crocus stigmas gives its name to a deep orange-yellow colour.

clue.text: Strong stocking material with a safety device

indicators.note: stocking means holding goods inside, so the word for strong holds the other letters

parts.note: firm means strong or solid
material means real, having substance

explanation.surface: A sturdy hosiery fabric comes with a safety device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking material' reads as nylon; 'stocking' means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren or bell that warns occupants of a blaze is a device fitted for safety.

clue.text: Old fogey, eighty-one perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a conventional, old-fashioned person, out of touch
81 is nine times nine, a number multiplied by itself

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person, maybe aged eighty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A conventional dull person is called this in slang, and a number times itself is this in arithmetic.

clue.text: Observe something other than a buzzer outside initially needed

indicators.note: outside means the phrase for something other than a buzzer goes round the next letter

parts.note: something other than a buzzing bee is literally not a bee

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word needed

explanation.surface: Pay attention to something that isn't a buzzer, which is first needed outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase, abbreviated NB, means 'note well', used to draw attention to something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is an instruction to note well, the same as an imperative to observe.

clue.text: Huge hole right behind box

indicators.note: behind places the abbreviation for right after the word for box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box for goods

explanation.surface: A huge hole is just to the right behind a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped cavity, as made by a meteor or volcano, is a very large hole in the ground.

clue.text: Libertine in cap of khaki, one covered in spots

indicators.note: covered in means the letters are wrapped by the word for spots

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top, its opening letter, here of khaki

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A womaniser wears a khaki cap while covered in pimples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Libertine' is used as an adjective, dissolute.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing but dissolute manner is that of a rake, so libertine and this adjective share a sense.

clue.text: Ultimately, glamour all there is about it: flash Italian resort

indicators.note: the word for all there is placed around 'it', the letter just picked

parts.note: someone all there is mentally sound, sane

indicators.note: ultimately picks the closing letter of the word glamour

parts.note: a flash is a moment, shortened to MO

explanation.surface: Glamour is the be-all and end-all of a flashy Italian holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers to the letter just picked from glamour; 'flash' is a moment, as in 'half a mo', not showiness.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Ligurian coast of the Italian Riviera is a well-known seaside resort.

clue.text: Work I need is yet to be rescheduled

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or knead it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A busy person's needed job has not yet been rescheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal term means adjourned with no future date fixed, so not yet set again.

clue.text: Run, don't walk beneath it!

definitions.meaning: a run is a line of unravelled stitches in tights
superstition says walking under a set of rungs leaning on a wall is unlucky

explanation.surface: A warning to hurry and avoid walking under something unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear in stockings is called this in Britain, and it is also the climbing frame that superstition forbids walking under.

clue.text: Completely covered in straw, a shed

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words straw, a shed

explanation.surface: Something is entirely buried in straw in a farm shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded or overflowing, a place swamped by water is covered entirely, and so too with anything else.

clue.text: Asian giant oak's last big acorn cracked

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word oak's
a cracked acorn is broken up, so its letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An enormous Asian oak's final big acorn splits open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian giant' seems to be the oak itself; it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest venomous snake, found in South and Southeast Asia, is a giant among serpents.

clue.text: A pair to hold up

definitions.meaning: a couple, as of game birds shot

explanation.surface: Two people stage a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple of shot pheasants is called this, and it also means to support with a strut.

clue.text: Aged don is awfully determined

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters are set out in disorder

explanation.surface: An elderly university teacher is dreadfully set in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'determined' looks like stubborn; it means identified, as a doctor does an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who has identified an illness from its symptoms has established or ascertained its nature.

clue.text: Decency in good people

parts.note: a race is a people or ethnic group

explanation.surface: Good people show decency.
explanation.definitionFit: The decency to apologise is the courtesy, the graciousness, to do so: a matching sense of politeness.

clue.text: Negligent fail again?

definitions.meaning: jokingly read as ..., to miss once more

explanation.surface: Is it careless to fail a second time?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone careless in their duties is neglectful, and the playful second reading splits the word as a repeated failure.

clue.text: Bottom Irish number, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the name of the tune is heard rather than written

parts.note: a number is a song or tune; the Londonderry Air, or Derry Air, is the tune of Danny Boy

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about which Irish song shares its name with the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Londonderry Air is the traditional Irish melody of 'Danny Boy'; Derry is the city of Londonderry in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French for 'behind', the word is a polite or jokey name for the buttocks.
